instructional_purpose: Introduces the abrogator class as a functional category of governors that cancel the all-nominative default of a noun-initial predication, and installs its first family through four high-frequency verbal members together with their inflectional behaviour. The lesson's second aim is to make the learner locate two distinct governed slots and state a case reason for each.
concepts_taught: the class label نواسخ defined by its case effect rather than by word class
the kana-family signature: the first governed element stays nominative, the second becomes accusative
the two slot labels اسم كان and خبر كان as role names, not positions
four introductory members: كان، أصبح، صار، ليس
aspect/temporal differentiation among those four members
person and number inflection of the members, including hollow-stem shortening
ليس as a member with no imperfective stem but present-time force
the substitution route for past-time negation using لم with the jussive
order latitude: the accusative element may precede the nominative one, and adjuncts may precede the governor

linguistic_propositions.proposition: A member of this verbal family leaves the first governed nominal in the nominative and imposes the accusative on the predicate element.
The item ليس has a defective paradigm: only perfective-shaped forms exist, inflecting for person and number but not for tense, while its semantic force is present-time negation.
Past-time negation of an attributive state is expressed by لم plus the jussive of the inflecting member rather than by the frozen negator.
Each member carries a distinct temporal or aspectual colouring: general past state, change of state anchored to morning, completed transformation, and present negation.
The members belong to different root classes (hollow, sound, defective), and the class determines the stem shape before consonant-initial subject affixes.
The accusative element may precede the nominative element, and material external to the predication may precede the governor, without disturbing the case assignment.
The nominative slot can be filled by the inflectional subject affix of the conjugated governor itself, in which case no independent nominative word is present.

recognition_criteria: an equative predication preceded by a member of the listed verbal roster
a single accusative-marked nominal or adjective after a verb of state where no transitive-object reading is available
a conjugated governor whose subject is realized only as an affix, leaving the accusative complement as the sole independently marked governed element
a present-time negated equative expressed by a perfective-shaped form of the defective member
procedures: identify the governor as a member of this family
assign the nominative element to the اسم slot and the accusative element to the خبر slot
verify that the accusative exponent sits on the predicate element and not on the subject
for past-time negation, switch from the frozen negator to the jussive-negation strategy on the inflecting member
select among the members according to the intended aspect: state, change, completed transformation, or negation
conditions: the regime applies over a nominal (equative) predication, not over a verbal one
the frozen member is presented as confined to present-time reference
the accusative exponent lands on the predicate word itself, whether that word is an adjective, a participle, or a noun
exceptions: the frozen member stands outside the tense inflection the other members show
hollow members shorten the stem and shift its vowel before consonant-initial subject affixes, unlike the sound member
when the subject is affixal there is no independent nominative word to inspect
contrasts: default equative predication (both elements nominative) against the governed one (predicate accusative)
the four members set against one another on an aspectual axis
present-time negation by the frozen member against past-time negation by jussive negation of the inflecting member
subject versus predicate as the target of the accusative, which is where the dominant learner error sits

common_mistakes.pattern: leaving the predicate element in the nominative after a family member
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the family's whole grammatical signature is the accusative it imposes on that element; leaving it nominative erases every trace of the governor
common_mistakes.correction_principle: after identifying the governor, relocate the expected accusative exponent onto the second governed element

common_mistakes.pattern: marking the first governed element accusative after a family member
common_mistakes.why_wrong: this inverts the signature and produces the pattern of the rival particle family instead
common_mistakes.correction_principle: the accusative belongs to exactly one of the two slots for this family, and it is the predicate slot

common_mistakes.pattern: using the frozen negator to express a past-time negation
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the item bears present-time force and has no way to host past reference
common_mistakes.correction_principle: route past-time negation through jussive negation of the inflecting member

common_mistakes.pattern: attempting to build an imperfective form of the frozen negator
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the item is defective and possesses no imperfective stem
common_mistakes.correction_principle: treat its paradigm as inflecting for person and number only

common_mistakes.pattern: stacking the frozen negator before a finite verb to negate it
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the negator governs a nominal predication and does not take a finite verb as its complement
common_mistakes.correction_principle: use a verb-negating particle for verbal predications

misleading_shortcuts: reading the accusative after these verbs as a direct object, which mis-analyses a state predicate as evidence of transitivity
taking the morning-anchored gloss of one member literally, when in ordinary prose that temporal component is largely bleached
treating predicate-before-subject order as freely available rather than as a conditioned option
presenting jussive negation as the only past-negation route, when negation of the perfective form is equally available and is not mentioned

instructional_purpose: Extends the verbal abrogator family with two subclasses the previous lesson did not reach: continuative members that are licensed only under a preceding negator, and time-anchored members that situate the state within a part of the day. It also widens the inventory of things that may occupy the predicate slot.
concepts_taught: a continuative subclass whose members lexically denote cessation and are inverted by negation
a time-anchored subclass locating the state at night, by day, in the evening, or in late morning
a duration member that subordinates a clause and takes a consequent
variation in the negating particle used with the continuative imperfective
four realizations of the predicate slot: single word, prepositional phrase, verbal clause, nominal clause
inflection of hollow and geminate members with their stem changes

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The continuative members are negative-polarity items: they yield the continuative sense only under a preceding negator, and the lesson also admits an oath or a prohibition as an alternative licenser.
The continuative reading is compositional — negation applied to a verb of ceasing produces a positive persistence reading.
Left unlicensed, a continuative member retains its literal cessation meaning and therefore asserts the opposite of what the learner intends.
The particle preceding the duration member is not negation but a masdar-forming particle with temporal force, so the composite means a span rather than a denial.
Two different negating particles are available with the imperfective of the leading continuative member with no difference in sense.
The time-anchored members carry a genuine time-of-day component in their lexical meaning.
The predicate slot of the whole family may be filled by a full clause, verbal or nominal, and not only by a single accusative-marked word.
The duration member heads a subordinate clause whose main clause supplies the consequent.

recognition_criteria: a negator immediately followed by a cessation verb, forming one governing unit over a nominal predication
the same governing behaviour as the core family — one nominative element, one accusative element — but with a two-token governor
a time-anchored member whose predicate names a state rather than an event
the duration composite followed by a predication and then by a consequent clause
a predicate slot occupied by a clause, in which case no case exponent is visible on it at all
procedures: check whether the candidate governor is a continuative member and, if so, whether a licenser precedes it
read the negator and the cessation verb as a single continuative governor rather than as negation of the sentence
distinguish the negating particle from the homographic subordinating particle by which member follows it
apply the same slot assignment as the core family once the governor is settled
classify the predicate realization before expecting any case exponent on it
conditions: continuative members require a preceding negator or an equivalent licenser to carry the persistence reading
the duration member requires its particle and a following consequent clause
the case signature of the core family carries over unchanged to both subclasses
exceptions: the same surface particle functions as negation before the continuative members but as a subordinating masdar particle before the duration member
the duration member is exhibited only in perfective shape, and the lesson does not say whether an imperfective is licensed
geminate and hollow members alter their stems before consonant-initial subject affixes
when the predicate is a clause there is no accusative exponent to observe, though the slot is the same
contrasts: cessation verb bare against cessation verb licensed by negation, which reverses the truth conditions
the negating use of the particle against its subordinating use with the duration member
the time-anchored members against one another along the parts of the day
single-word predicates against phrasal and clausal predicates, which differ in whether case is visible

common_mistakes.pattern: using a continuative member without its licensing negator
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the bare verb asserts cessation, so the sentence states the reverse of the intended persistence
common_mistakes.correction_principle: treat the licenser as part of the governor rather than as optional sentence-level negation

common_mistakes.pattern: confusing the perfective of the night-anchored member with a segmentally similar common noun
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the two are unrelated lexical items from different categories, and the confusion produces a category error rather than a case error
common_mistakes.correction_principle: identify the token's part of speech from its position and inflection before glossing it

common_mistakes.pattern: using the duration composite as an ordinary sentence negator
common_mistakes.why_wrong: its particle is not negation there, and the construction requires a consequent clause that plain negation does not
common_mistakes.correction_principle: test for the consequent clause: its absence means the reading is not the duration one

common_mistakes.pattern: leaving the predicate nominative after a continuative governor
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the subclass inherits the case signature of the core family without alteration
common_mistakes.correction_principle: the two-token governor governs exactly as a single-token member of the same family does

misleading_shortcuts: reading the negator in a continuative governor as negating the whole sentence, which flips the intended meaning
treating every occurrence of the ambiguous particle before this family as negation, when one member selects the subordinating counterpart instead
taking the time-of-day glosses as literal restrictions in modern prose, where several of these members are largely bleached
assuming the accusative is always observable on the predicate, when a clausal predicate shows no exponent at all

instructional_purpose: Installs the second abrogator family — particles whose case effect is the exact mirror of the verbal family taught earlier — and differentiates its first three members not by case behaviour, which they share, but by clause position and by the environment that selects each one.
concepts_taught: the particle family and its inverted case signature: first element accusative, predicate nominative
the slot labels اسم إنّ and خبر إنّ

linguistic_propositions.proposition: This family assigns the accusative to the first governed element and leaves the predicate nominative, exactly reversing the verbal family's signature.
The emphatic member must stand at the head of its clause.
The subordinating member links a nominal clause to a preceding verb of knowing, thinking, saying, or perceiving, and the resulting clause serves as that verb's complement.
After a verb of saying, the subordinating member is required and the emphatic member is an error.
The geminate adversative particle must be followed by a noun or an enclitic pronoun; before a finite verb the non-geminate counterpart is used instead and does not govern.
An enclitic pronoun attached to the particle occupies the accusative slot.
The predicate slot may be filled by a verbal clause rather than by a single nominative word.
Because these items are particles, they carry no inflection and their shape is invariant across subjects.

recognition_criteria: a clause-initial particle of this roster followed immediately by an accusative-marked nominal
a nominative-marked predicate following that nominal, which is the diagnostic that distinguishes this family from the verbal one
the particle carrying an enclitic pronoun, in which case the accusative slot has no independent word
a geminate adversative particle whose complement is nominal, as against its non-geminate counterpart whose complement is verbal
procedures: identify the particle and confirm it belongs to this roster
assign the accusative to the element immediately following and the nominative to the predicate
select the member by environment: clause-initial emphasis, post-cognition-verb subordination, or adversative contrast
before a finite verb, switch the adversative to its non-geminate form and stop expecting government
when the particle bears an enclitic, treat that enclitic as the accusative element
conditions: the emphatic member is licensed only clause-initially
the subordinating member is licensed by a preceding governor that selects a clausal complement
the geminate adversative is licensed only before a nominal or an enclitic pronoun
the case signature applies over a nominal predication
exceptions: the same lexical content appears in a governing geminate shape and a non-governing non-geminate shape, and only the former assigns case
an enclitic pronoun leaves no independently case-marked accusative word to inspect
a clausal predicate carries no visible nominative exponent
contrasts: the verbal family against the particle family as mirror images of one another
emphatic against subordinating member, separated by clause position and by the presence of a selecting verb
geminate against non-geminate adversative, separated by the category of what follows
inflecting verbal governors against invariant particle governors

common_mistakes.pattern: leaving the first element nominative after a particle of this family
common_mistakes.why_wrong: it preserves the default pattern and so leaves the governor without any effect, and it also collides with the verbal family's signature
common_mistakes.correction_principle: the accusative attaches to the element immediately governed by the particle, not to the predicate

common_mistakes.pattern: marking the predicate accusative after a particle of this family
common_mistakes.why_wrong: it imports the verbal family's signature into a family whose defining property is the opposite assignment
common_mistakes.correction_principle: identify the family before assigning any case, since membership alone decides which slot receives the accusative

common_mistakes.pattern: interchanging the emphatic and subordinating members
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the two are selected by different environments, and the choice carries a difference in clause status rather than in emphasis alone
common_mistakes.correction_principle: let clause position and the presence of a selecting verb decide the member

common_mistakes.pattern: placing the geminate adversative before a finite verb
common_mistakes.why_wrong: that particle requires a nominal complement, so a verb leaves its accusative slot unfillable
common_mistakes.correction_principle: use the non-geminate counterpart before a verb, or attach an enclitic pronoun and keep the geminate form

misleading_shortcuts: reading the accusative after these particles as a direct object, since the governor is not a verb and there is no transitivity involved
treating the two members as freely interchangeable stylistic variants
assuming any surface occurrence of the adversative string governs, when only the geminate shape does
expecting the family signature to be visible on every occurrence, when enclitics and clausal predicates hide one exponent or the other

instructional_purpose: Completes the particle family with three members that share the established case signature exactly and are therefore taught purely as a semantic discrimination task: resemblance, counterfactual wish, and attainable hope. The grammatical content is a restatement; the instructional content is modal choice.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: All three members assign the accusative to the first governed element and leave the predicate nominative, identically to the members taught earlier.
One member marks a desire presented as unattainable or contrary to fact.
A second member marks an outcome presented as attainable, and the two are distinguished by the speaker's assessment of likelihood rather than by any structural difference.
The resemblance member asserts a comparison stronger than the ordinary comparative preposition or the comparison noun, and is reserved for emphatic or poetic use.
Enclitic pronouns attach to all three members and occupy the accusative slot.
The predicate slot of these members may be a verbal clause.

recognition_criteria: any of the three particles heading a nominal predication, with the following element accusative
a nominative predicate as the confirmation that the particle family, not the verbal family, is at work
the particle carrying an enclitic pronoun as its governed element
for the modal reading specifically, the surrounding discourse rather than any structural cue

for production, choose between the wish and hope members according to whether the state of affairs is presented as attainable
reserve the resemblance member for emphatic comparison and use the ordinary comparison devices otherwise
attach the enclitic directly to the particle when the governed element is pronominal

instructional_purpose: Introduces the third abrogator type: cognition verbs that absorb a whole predication as two accusative complements while retaining their own nominative agent. The lesson's distinctive work is the subdivision of the roster by epistemic strength and the recognition that two of its members govern this way only under one of their senses.

the evidential colouring of one member, which signals speaker distance from the claim

persistence of both accusatives under negation

linguistic_propositions.proposition: These verbs take two accusative complements which correspond to the subject and predicate of an embedded predication.
The verb keeps its own agent in the nominative, so the clause contains one nominative and two accusatives rather than the two-element pattern of the other families.
The roster divides into verbs expressing supposition and verbs expressing certainty, a division of meaning that does not affect the case assignment.
Two members take two complements only in their judgemental sense; in their literal perception or location sense they take a single complement.
One member of the supposition group implies that the speaker doubts the reported claim.
An enclitic pronoun on the verb realizes the first complement, with the second complement following as a separate word.
Negating the verb leaves both complements accusative.
A complement slot may be filled by a clause rather than by a single accusative word.

recognition_criteria: a cognition verb followed by two accusative-marked elements neither of which is a circumstantial or adverbial accusative
a separate nominative agent, which is the surface cue that separates this family from the other two
for the sense-conditioned members, a second accusative that predicates something of the first rather than merely naming a further participant
an enclitic on the verb plus one following accusative, which is the same structure with the first slot hidden

assign the first complement to the embedded subject and the second to the embedded predicate

when the verb bears an enclitic, count that enclitic as the first complement

the second complement must predicate of the first; otherwise the structure is not this one
the agent slot is filled independently of the two complements
exceptions: the two sense-conditioned members take a single complement in their literal sense
an enclitic first complement leaves only one independently marked accusative visible

common_mistakes.pattern: applying the particle family's split assignment to these verbs

common_mistakes.correction_principle: let the sense determine the complement count rather than the lemma

common_mistakes.pattern: treating the doubt-implying member as epistemically neutral
common_mistakes.why_wrong: it signals the speaker's distance from the claim, so using it flattens or reverses the intended stance
common_mistakes.correction_principle: select among the roster by epistemic stance, using the certainty group for asserted knowledge and the neutral supposition verb for plain conjecture

instructional_purpose: A synthesis lesson that converts three separately learned governance regimes into one ordered identification task: recognize the governor, classify its family, then apply that family's case signature. It also introduces stacking, where several abrogators occupy one sentence and each governs its own pair.
concepts_taught: an ordered decision procedure that puts family identification before any case assignment
a single comparison table holding all three signatures side by side

stacking of abrogators within one sentence, with each governor owning its own pair
predicate realizations across all three families: single word, prepositional phrase, verbal clause
negated and compound forms of a verbal family member appearing inside analysis
sense-conditioned complement count restated as a standing confusion point

linguistic_propositions.proposition: All three families share one abstract effect — cancelling the all-nominative default — and differ only in which slots receive the accusative.
Family identity, not the individual lexical item, determines the case assignment, so classification must precede assignment.
The cognition family is distinguished on the surface by having a nominative agent in addition to its two accusative complements.
Several abrogators may occur in one sentence, each governing its own pair, and the lesson exhibits a three-governor chain.
A verbal-family member may take a following imperfective verb as its predicate, yielding a compound temporal reading.
A prepositional phrase may occupy the predicate slot, in which case no case exponent appears on it.
The mnemonic that a verb 'prefers' an accusative complement while a particle 'seizes' the subject explains the split between the first two families.

recognition_criteria: a governor drawn from one of the three consolidated rosters
the governor's word class — inflecting verb against invariant particle — as the first cut
the presence or absence of a separate nominative agent as the cut between the two verbal families
the count and placement of accusative exponents as confirmation rather than as the identification cue
for stacked cases, a second governor inside the predicate of the first

common_mistakes.pattern: swapping the assignments of the verbal and particle families
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the two are exact mirror images, so a swap yields a fully well-formed-looking sentence with both exponents wrong
common_mistakes.correction_principle: identify the governor's word class first; the case follows from the family and not from the position of the word

common_mistakes.pattern: treating the cognition verb's agent as one of the accusatives
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the agent is the one who thinks or knows and is not part of the absorbed predication
common_mistakes.correction_principle: count three nominals for this family and assign the nominative to the agent before touching the complements

common_mistakes.pattern: applying a two-complement expectation to a literal perception or location use
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the complement count depends on the sense, not on the lemma
common_mistakes.correction_principle: settle the sense before counting complements

common_mistakes.pattern: assigning a single family's signature across a sentence that contains more than one governor
common_mistakes.why_wrong: each governor governs only its own pair, so a blanket assignment corrupts the elements belonging to the other governor
common_mistakes.correction_principle: resolve governors one at a time with explicit scope for each
